## Analysis

### **Define the primary hypothesis**

**Research question:** Does gene expression differ between tumour and normal breast tissue?

### Loading libraries

```{r}
library(tidyverse)
library(broom)
```

### Creating a long augment data

We need to create the long augment data so that have all the genes defined in one column. This way we are able to group the data by gene. The clean augment data should contain genes instead of probes.

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long <- pivot_longer(data = gravier_clean_aug,
                                       cols= -state, #state will be either tumor or normal
                                       names_to = "genes", 
                                       values_to = "expression")
```

### Group by gene

Creating a dplyr pipeline, use the group_by() function to group your gravier_clean_aug_long dataset by gene and then add the nest() to your pipeline.

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long |> 
  group_by(genes) |>
  nest()
```

### Adding a new variable model object

Using the map()-function, add a new line to your pipeline, where you add a new variable model_object to your gravier_clean_aug_long_nested dataset, which R will compute *per* gene.

```{r}
model_object <- model_object |>  
                tidy(conf.int = TRUE,
                conf.level = 0.95)
```

#### Tidying the model object

```{r}
gravier_clean_aug_long_nested <- gravier_clean_aug_long_nested |>
   ungroup() |>
  mutate(model_object_tidy = map(.x = model_object,
                   .f = ~ tidy(.x, conf.int = TRUE, conf.level = 0.95)))
```
